distinct_character_theorem.character_family: q_sigma = tau^{z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma)} = exp((z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma)) log(tau))
proof_steps: 1. Fix one nontrivial zero rho_0 = 1/2 + z_{rho_0}.
2. Suppose toward a contradiction that {q_sigma : zeta(sigma) = 0} takes only finitely many values {w_1, ..., w_M}.

3. Since exp(z log(tau)) = exp(z' log(tau)) iff z - z' in (2*pi*i / log(tau)) Z, each value w_j restricts Re(z_sigma) to a single value and Im(z_sigma) = gamma_sigma to a single vertical arithmetic progression gamma_0^{(j)} + (2*pi / log(tau)) Z.
4. A finite union of M vertical arithmetic progressions with spacing 2*pi / log(tau) contains at most M * (T * log(tau) / pi + 2) = O(T) points with |gamma_sigma| <= T.

5. By the Riemann-von Mangoldt zero-counting theorem N(T) = (T/(2*pi)) log(T/(2*pi)) - T/(2*pi) + O(log T) (von Mangoldt 1905; Titchmarsh 1986, Theorem 9.4; Trudgian 2014), the number of nontrivial zeros up to height T grows as (T/(2*pi)) log(T/(2*pi)) = Omega(T log T), contradicting O(T).
6. Therefore {q_sigma} contains infinitely many distinct nonzero complex numbers != 1.

finite_laurent_projector_status.laurent_root_bound: Multiplying P_N(q) by q^N gives a polynomial Q_{2N}(q) = q^N P_N(q) of degree <= 2N. Since Q_{2N}(q) vanishes on infinitely many distinct values q_sigma (in particular on at least 2N + 1 distinct values), Q_{2N} = 0 identically, forcing all c_K = 0 and P_N(1) = 0.

finite_differential_projector_status.differential_filter_form: p(d/dr) e^{r lambda} = p(lambda) e^{r lambda},  p(lambda) = sum_{m=0}^M a_m lambda^m

finite_differential_projector_status.distinct_exponent_argument: For fixed rho_0, the nontrivial zeros sigma have infinitely many distinct ordinates gamma_sigma (since N(T) -> infty and every zero has finite multiplicity), yielding infinitely many distinct nonzero pair exponents lambda_{rho_0, sigma} = (z_{rho_0} + conj(z_sigma)) log(tau). A polynomial p of degree <= M vanishing on more than M distinct points must satisfy p = 0 identically, forcing p(0) = 0.
finite_differential_projector_status.rational_filter_extension: For any finite rational filter R(lambda) = p(lambda)/q(lambda) analytic at lambda = 0 (so q(0) != 0 and R(0) = p(0)/q(0) != 0), vanishing on all nonstationary pair exponents lambda_{rho_0, sigma} outside the finite pole set of q still forces the polynomial numerator p(lambda) to have infinitely many distinct roots, hence p = 0 and R = 0.

pontryagin_audit.unitary_dual_characters: q = e^{i theta} in T (for Z) or e^{i r omega} with omega in R (for R)
pontryagin_audit.boundedness_criterion: exp(r lambda) is bounded on R (or Z) iff Re(lambda) = 0
pontryagin_audit.single_zero_character_scope: For a single-zero character chi_z(K) = tau^{K z}, boundedness/unitarity on Z or R holds iff Re(z) = delta_rho = 0, which IS the Riemann Hypothesis for rho.
pontryagin_audit.pair_character_scope: For the sesquilinear common-shift pair character tau^{r(z_rho + conj(z_sigma))}, boundedness/unitarity for ALL pairs (rho, sigma)—and in particular for the diagonal pair sigma = rho where z_rho + conj(z_rho) = 2 delta_rho—holds iff every delta_rho = 0. Therefore, invoking Pontryagin character orthogonality or an invariant mean on Z or R to annihilate all nonstationary pair characters implicitly assumes delta_rho = 0.

complex_grade_audit.complex_grade_parameter: K = v exp(i theta),  v in R
complex_grade_audit.modulus_formula: |tau^{K lambda}| = exp(v log(tau) (cos(theta) Re(lambda) - sin(theta) Im(lambda)))
complex_grade_audit.obstruction_proof: For off-diagonal pairs with Im(lambda) = gamma_rho - gamma_sigma != 0 and Re(lambda) = 0, bilateral boundedness in v requires sin(theta) = 0 (theta in pi Z, the real grade axis). On the real grade axis sin(theta) = 0, cos(theta) = +-1, so any off-critical diagonal pair with Re(lambda) = 2 delta_rho != 0 has growth rate +-2 delta_rho != 0. Since sin^2(theta) + cos^2(theta) = 1, no fixed zero-independent angle theta can simultaneously make both families unitary.
